decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete standalone main-board layer count and records that it no longer applies under the integrated-board architecture.

The integrated-board transition requires updating architecture-specific descriptions, but the existing Event incorrectly omits the previously included SK6812 LEDs despite the client's requirement to retain the same functionality.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I was thinking, if you have time for a new project and are willing to do it, that we try to make as cheap as possible single board for this project. So everything will be on one board and from start we try to match JLCPCB Basica component (as much as possible). It will have much less connectors as there are no interboard connectors. Also if you have some idea on how to make something better/cheaper but have same functionality you can suggest. I can add it as new milestone to this project and we can agree on price. What do you think does it make sense?

value_updates.normal_operation_role: Primary source for the ESP32-S3, INA219, downstream 3.3V sensors, I2C display, TTP223, AM312, and SK6812 addressable LEDs in the single integrated-board architecture
value_updates.voltage_compensation_purpose: Compensate for the integrated-board Schottky-diode OR-ing drop so the system rail remains at 3.3V under all conditions

decisions.reason: The antenna-edge placement remains unchanged, and the existing same-message MODIFY already transfers its scope to the integrated-board context.
The AXP2101 thermal-pad requirement remains valid without a value change, and the existing same-message MODIFY already adds the integrated-board context.

The client eliminates interboard connectors while retaining functionality; the panel connectors remain, but the power-button entry must retain its identity while removing its obsolete dependency on the interboard J_PWR_SIG connector.
